name: SG Finserve Ltd
title: SG Finserve Ltd - 539199 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Nil-NPA supply-chain NBFC posts record Q1 PBT of INR72 crore and loan book INR4,552 crore; management guides FY27 PBT ~INR300 crore, but no capacity or supply-side cycle signal since this is a lender, not an industrial.

summary.headline: SG Finserve posts record Q1 FY27 PBT of INR72 crore (+27% QoQ) and loan book of INR4,552 crore (+82% YoY) with nil NPAs.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly PBT of INR72 crore, up 27% QoQ, with the loan book rising 16% QoQ to INR4,552 crore. Net worth reached INR1,539 crore, leverage moved to 2.2x from 1.9x at March 2026, and CRAR stood at 32%. Annualised ROA was 5.1% and ROE 14%, with nil NPAs reported. Management reiterated FY27 PBT visibility of about INR300 crore (about 75% YoY), with AUM guidance of INR5,500 crore for FY27 and a 25-30% AUM CAGR over three to four years.

segments.name: Supply chain finance and working capital
segments.commentary: Management said about two-thirds of business financing sits in working capital, supply chain and factoring; about one-third of AUM is from the APL Apollo ecosystem, down from a higher share, and 52 anchor mandates are running (5 added in Q1).

segments.name: Factoring (TReDS and bilateral)
segments.commentary: Factoring outstanding was INR225 crore in June versus INR175 crore in March; commercialised in March-April 2026, with yields at par with channel finance for TReDS and at or slightly above for bilateral deals.

segments.name: Beyond supply chain (cross-sell LAP, opportunistic)
segments.commentary: Roughly one-third of business financing; management named digital lending and loan against property as products under consideration, with no retail or consumer lending.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PBT visibility of about INR300 crore (about 75% YoY); PAT about INR225 crore; FY27 closing equity about INR1,700 crore; FY27 AUM about INR5,500 crore (management called INR6,000 crore aspirational).
Targeted AUM CAGR of 25-30% over three to four years, with profitability CAGR of 30-35%; INR10,000 crore AUM now targeted for FY30 (earlier guidance was INR7,500 crore for FY30) and possibly FY29.
Quarter-on-quarter growth normalised to about 8-10% for PAT, with AUM growth of about 15-16% QoQ, after adjusting for INR337 crore equity received at end-March and early April.
Cost-to-income to be kept below 15%; opex maintained at about 1% of average book.
Leverage to move from 2x towards 3x over about two years, taking ROE from 14% towards 16% with ROA held at around 4.5-5%. No equity raise planned through the growth phase up to INR10,000 crore AUM.
Insurance broking subsidiary (SG Insurance Brokers) incorporated; IRDAI licence pending, commercialisation at least two to three quarters away, and not expected before Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: No capex or physical capacity discussed; the business is asset-light, with about 30 locations for sales coverage.
ESOP pool of 20 lakh approved by shareholders; about 10.32 lakh granted in April and about 50,000 granted in July to new joiners, leaving about 9 lakh unallocated with no timing decided.
GIFT City entity approval received from the board, subject to dual RBI and IFSCA approvals; long-term plan.
Board has approved AIF and ARC business; no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Average portfolio yield held at about 12.5% in Q3, Q4 and Q1, with factoring added without diluting or enhancing the overall yield.
Management said geopolitical uncertainty is hitting the MSME and trader business through lower incremental working capital needs, but has not yet translated into credit pressure.

Management said it does not compete with large banks and NBFCs, and fills the gap left when a dealer's bank working capital limit falls short of its requirement; for example, INR2 crore gap on a INR10 crore need.
Management estimated the addressable market as receivables of about INR25 lakh crore on the balance sheets of the top 1,000 corporates.
Management said the MoU-based anchor pipeline (52 anchors, INR7,700 crore MoU value) is a dummy limit and should not be read as book visibility.

qa_highlights.question: Will equity be raised this year, given net worth near INR1,510 crore and projected FY27 book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity raise is needed; net worth is INR1,539 crore at 30 June, and FY27 closing equity should be about INR1,700 crore, with leverage rising from 2x towards 3x over about two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 AUM guidance only 25-30% CAGR when growth is far higher currently?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called itself a conservative lender, citing the aim of nil NPAs, low credit cost and a balance sheet able to absorb shocks; 25-30% AUM CAGR is described as healthy and sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Is NPA-free status sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nil NPA is the stated aim, but acknowledged that losses can occur in lending; a larger net worth and profitability would be the buffer.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q1 run rate persist, given that H2 is usually stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR4,000 crore average book sustains the base, with incremental growth on top; QoQ PAT growth of 8-10% is targeted after normalising the equity infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cost-to-income only 7% against a 14% guide?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified the right metric is opex at about 1% of average book, and the company guides to cost-to-income below 15%.

qa_highlights.question: What is SG Insurance Brokers and when will it start?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a wholly owned subsidiary for B2B fee-based cross-sell to the existing anchor and borrower ecosystem, not underwriting; subject to IRDAI approval and at least two to three quarters away.

risks_watch: Credit risk without NPAs: management concedes losses can occur, and nil NPA is a stated aim, not a guarantee.
Geopolitical stress on MSME and trader working-capital demand could slow new business growth, though credit costs are so far unaffected.
Q1 PBT was boosted by equity received in late March and April (INR337 crore), so QoQ growth should normalise to about 8-10%.
Guidance has been raised in substance (INR10,000 crore AUM by FY30 versus INR7,500 crore earlier), so next-quarter delivery against the INR5,500 crore FY27 AUM target should be tracked.
Insurance broking and factoring scale-up depend on regulatory approvals and team build-out; factoring is still small (about 5% of AUM).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the reported numbers and visibility, but deliberately conservative on forward growth: management repeatedly declined to raise AUM guidance beyond 25-30% CAGR and called INR6,000 crore FY27 AUM aspirational. Evasive on the MoU anchor figures and on the exact ESOP timing.
key_quotes: We are a conservative lender. That conservatism is reflecting in our NPAs and credit cost.
Our mission number one is that we ensure zero NPAs.
So, up to INR10,000 crores of AUM, we don't need any equity.

financial_highlights.change: from INR175 crore in March (+INR50 crore)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 PBT of about INR300 crore (about 75% YoY) and FY27 AUM of about INR5,500 crore, backed by the current run rate, 52 anchor mandates and a factoring book that grew INR50 crore in Q1, but no physical capacity is being added and the anchor MoU pipeline is explicitly a dummy limit, so backing is only partial.
